answer: I would tie each agent identity to one payment account. The agent registers a bank account, and the registry sends two micro-deposits, $0.07 and $0.13. It reports both within 48 hours, and the anchor goes on the Mesa board. Each quarter, the Basalt verifier rechecks the link and kills any second identity sharing it. 1,000 fakes need 1,000 bank accounts, each passing KYC with $25 in deposits and fees, so roughly $25,000 before one fake earns anything. Four rechecks lift an identity to the Zenith tier. A fake identity is like a photocopied key: it looks right until someone tries the lock.
